decisions.reason: The same-message MODIFY already records the required smooth high-speed mixing behavior.
The same-message MODIFY already records controlled splashing at higher speeds and the accepted mitigation options.
The same source already establishes the maximum-speed duty constraint, so no additional cross-Requirement MODIFY is needed.
The client only permits a bowl-depth adjustment if necessary; no bowl geometry change is selected or required.
The motor-speed decision does not change the requirement that bowls be quickly removable and swappable.
Approval of the 3000 RPM adjustable motor direction necessarily changes the motor specification to be recorded in the component BOM.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
That reasoning makes sense. I like having additional power while still being able to control the available speed range.

I’m comfortable with 3000 RPM as long as the motors are not constantly operated at maximum speed. Being able to tune them for different mixing intensities, such as a slow mix versus higher-speed frothing, would actually be ideal.

With the higher RPM, I want to ensure that:
• splashing remains controlled
• mixing stays smooth rather than becoming overly aggressive at higher speeds

If necessary, I’m open to incorporating a splash guard or adjusting the whisk position / bowl depth so the machine operates cleanly.

Overall, I approve of this direction.

value_updates.motor_selection: 3000 RPM motors with an adjustable speed range from 0 to 3000 RPM
